home.metaTitle: Do I need a commercial license?
home.title: A commercial license for PineForge Codegen
home.lead: PineForge Codegen is free for personal trading and for noncommercial purposes. Using it for an organization, for other people's capital, inside a product or service you offer, or in a hosted service is Commercial Use, which needs a commercial license.
home.coversIntro: The LICENSE lists four uses that are Commercial Use. A commercial license permits them for the scope you buy:

uses.1: Managing, advising on, or trading capital that belongs to any other person or entity, whether or not for a fee.
uses.2: Use by, for, or on behalf of a company, fund, partnership, or other organization, including an individual's work for one.
uses.3: Embedding the software, or output generated by it, into a product or service made available to others.
uses.4: Operating a hosted, software-as-a-service, or otherwise public-facing service that uses the software.

home.plansIntro: Three plans map onto those uses: {team} covers use (2) for one organization; {fund} adds use (1), others' capital, priced by assets under management; {oem} covers uses (3) and (4), products and hosted services. Anything outside the bands is quoted.
home.notCovered: Personal trading with your own capital, for your own account, stays free under the LICENSE's Additional Permission. Noncommercial purposes stay free under the base license. A commercial license does not let you redistribute the transpiler as a standalone product.

guide.heading: Do I need one?
guide.intro: Answer a few questions about how you use PineForge Codegen. The guide follows the LICENSE and quotes the sentence each answer rests on.
guide.disclaimer: Not legal advice; the <license>LICENSE</license> is the controlling text; ask <email>enterprise@pineforge.dev</email> if unsure.
guide.askFirstAlso: Your answers also name use {uses}, quoted below with the rest. Name them in your message too: the written answer will cover every use you describe.
guide.licenseLink: Read the full LICENSE on GitHub

othersCapital.text: Will you manage, advise on, or trade capital that belongs to any other person or entity, whether or not for a fee?

organization.text: Will you use it by, for, or on behalf of a company, fund, partnership, or other organization, including your work for one?

noncommercialOrg.text: Is the organization a charitable organization, educational institution, public research organization, public safety or health organization, environmental protection organization, or government institution?
noncommercialOrg.hint: Asked after a yes to use (2). These are the organizations the base license's Noncommercial Organizations clause names.

embedding.text: Will you embed the software, or output generated by it, into a product or service made available to others?
embedding.hint: LICENSE use (3). Output includes the C++ the transpiler generates.

hosted.text: Will you operate a hosted, software-as-a-service, or otherwise public-facing service that uses the software?

naturalPerson.text: Are you an individual (a natural person) using it to research, develop, backtest, or execute trades in financial instruments?
naturalPerson.hint: The Personal Trading permission covers natural persons only.

ownAccount.text: Are the trades placed for your own account?

ownCapital.text: Are the trades funded solely by your own capital?

noncommercial.text: Is your use for a noncommercial purpose of your own, such as personal study, research or experiment for the benefit of public knowledge, a hobby, an amateur pursuit, or religious observance, without any anticipated commercial application?
noncommercial.hint: Personal uses that the PolyForm Noncommercial base license makes permitted purposes.

commercial-team.title: You need a commercial license: Team
commercial-team.body: Use by, for, or on behalf of an organization is Commercial Use. The Team plan covers one organization's internal use by its named users.

commercial-fund.title: You need a commercial license: Fund
commercial-fund.body: Managing, advising on, or trading other people's capital is Commercial Use. The Fund plan covers it, together with use for your organization, priced by assets under management.

commercial-oem.title: You need a commercial license: OEM / Embedded
commercial-oem.body: Embedding the software or its output in a product or service for others, or running a hosted or public-facing service with it, is Commercial Use. The OEM / Embedded plan covers it, scoped by products and end users. It covers use (2), use for your organization, only as far as needed to build and run those products and services: an organization that also uses the software for its own research or trading needs a Team plan as well, or a quote.

commercial-quote.title: You need a commercial license that no single plan covers
commercial-quote.body: Your answers combine uses that none of the self-serve plans covers on its own. Ask for a quote and describe your use.

ask-first.title: Ask us first
ask-first.body: The LICENSE contains both readings. The base license's Noncommercial Organizations clause makes use by such an organization a permitted purpose. The supplemental section says the uses in (1)–(4), including use (2) by, for, or on behalf of an organization, are Commercial Use, and the LICENSE says the supplemental sections control in a conflict. Counsel has not settled which reading applies. Before you rely on either, write to enterprise@pineforge.dev for a written answer.

personal-trading.title: No commercial license needed: Personal Trading
personal-trading.body: Research, development, backtesting, and trading by a natural person, for their own account and with their own capital, is Personal Trading, which the LICENSE permits free of charge.

permitted-noncommercial.title: No commercial license needed: a permitted purpose
permitted-noncommercial.body: Noncommercial purposes are permitted purposes under the base license, free of charge.

commercial-other.title: Your use needs a commercial license
commercial-other.body: Your use is neither Personal Trading nor a noncommercial purpose, so the free permissions do not cover it. Ask for a quote and describe your use.

static.heading: How the guide decides
static.rule1: Questions {use1}, {use2}, {use3} and {use4} are the four uses the LICENSE names as Commercial Use. A yes to any of them means you need a commercial license: Team for use (2) alone; Fund when you also handle others' capital (1); OEM / Embedded for products (3) and hosted services (4). A combination no single plan covers needs a quote.
static.ruleOrg: Question {org} is asked only after a yes to question {use2}: is the organization one of those the base license's Noncommercial Organizations clause names? If it is, the LICENSE contains two readings that counsel has not settled, so the guide recommends no plan, whatever else you answer, and asks you to write to us first.
static.rule2: If all four uses are no, questions {pt1} to {pt3} test Personal Trading: an individual, trading for their own account, with only their own capital. Three yes answers: no commercial license is needed.
static.rule3: Otherwise question {nc} asks whether your use is a personal noncommercial purpose under the base license. Yes: no commercial license is needed. No: ask for a commercial license.

plans.title: Plans
plans.lead: Each plan is a 12-month commercial license for PineForge Codegen. Prices are per year, for the scope shown.
plans.placeholders: Prices are placeholders, and no real payment is taken while the site is in preview.

team.permits: Use by, for, or on behalf of one organization: internal research, backtesting, and trading with the organization's own capital, by its named users (seats).
team.notCovered: Managing others' capital, embedding in a product, or a hosted service.

fund.permits: Managing, advising on, or trading others' capital, plus use for your organization, within an assets-under-management band. Includes the seats shown. Internal use only.
fund.notCovered: Embedding in a product or a hosted service for third parties.

oem.permits: Embedding the software or its output in a product or service made available to others, or operating a hosted, SaaS, or public-facing service with it, within the products and end users shown.
oem.notCovered: Managing, advising on, or trading others' capital (use 1); the licensee's own research and trading beyond building and running the licensed products; redistributing the transpiler as a standalone product.

plans.quoteBody: More seats, a larger fund, more products or end users, or a use none of these plans names: describe it and we will quote.

verify.title: Verify a license
verify.lead: Check a PineForge Codegen commercial license by its id, or check a signed license file. Only public details are shown: licensee company and country, plan, scope, and term.

status.valid: Valid: a genuine commercial license, active today.
status.validTest: Valid test license: genuine, but issued from a Stripe test-mode payment, so it is not a commercial license.
status.revoked: Revoked: this license no longer evidences a commercial license.
status.expired: Expired: the license term has ended.
status.not_yet_valid: Not yet valid: the license term has not started.
status.test_mode: Test license: issued from a Stripe test-mode payment; not a commercial license.
status.invalid_signature: Invalid signature: the license was changed after it was signed, or PineForge did not sign it. Do not rely on it.
status.unknown_key: Unknown signing key: the signature was not made with a key this site trusts.
status.not_found: Not found: no license with this id is on record, or the record differs from this file.
status.malformed: Not a license: this is not a signed PineForge Codegen license.
status.error: The check could not be completed. Try again in a moment.

verify.offline: The signed file can also be checked offline: it carries an Ed25519 signature over the canonical form of its license object, and the public keys are published at <link>/.well-known/pineforge-license-keys.json</link>. Revocation is only visible online.

who.a: Anyone whose use is Commercial Use under the LICENSE: managing, advising on, or trading others' capital; use by, for, or on behalf of an organization, including an individual's work for one; embedding the software or its output in a product or service for others; or operating a hosted or public-facing service with it. The decision guide on the home page walks through it. The LICENSE is the controlling text.

personal.a: Yes. Use by a natural person to research, develop, backtest, and execute trades for their own account, funded solely by their own capital, is Personal Trading, which the LICENSE permits free of charge. Noncommercial purposes are free under the base license too.

seats.a: A seat is a named user of the software under your license. How seats are counted and reassigned is set by the Commercial License Agreement. If you need more seats than a plan lists, ask for a quote.

aum.q: How are assets under management measured?
aum.a: The Fund plans are priced by the band your assets under management fall in. How and when AUM is measured is set by the Commercial License Agreement. If you are near a band edge, or above the largest band, write to enterprise@pineforge.dev.

upgrade.q: Can I upgrade or change my plan?
upgrade.a: Write to enterprise@pineforge.dev with your license id. Changes during a term are handled under the Commercial License Agreement.

renewal.a: Checkout is a one-time payment for a 12-month term, shown on your certificate. Nothing renews automatically: buy again before the end date, or write to enterprise@pineforge.dev.

invoice.q: Do I get an invoice? What about tax?
invoice.a: For a live purchase, Stripe creates an invoice for the payment; whether Stripe emails it to you depends on the seller's Stripe settings. Test-mode orders, including every order while the site is in preview, get no real invoice. Stripe asks for a billing address, lets you add a tax id, and shows the amount due before you pay.

refund.a: Refunds are as stated in the Commercial License Agreement. When an order is refunded in full, its license is revoked and the verify page reports it as revoked.

verify.q: What is the license id, and how is a license verified?
verify.a: Each license has an id like PFL-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX and a signed license file (JSON) carrying an Ed25519 signature. Anyone can check the id or the file on the verify page, which also reports revocation. The certificate page shows the same details in a printable form.

data.q: What information does the license contain?
data.a: The license names the licensee company and country, the plan and scope, the term, and the agreement version. It never contains the buyer's name or email; those stay with the order.

advice.a: No. The LICENSE and the Commercial License Agreement are the controlling texts. If you are unsure whether your use needs a license, write to enterprise@pineforge.dev.

preview.a: Not yet. While the site is in preview, prices are placeholders, no real payment is taken, and test licenses are not commercial licenses.
